Sentence (English): Unlike many others, I thought the installation process was the best thing about this purchase.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY THE BOSCH 300 DISHWASHER! ] || ---------------- || Unlike many others, I thought the installation process was the best thing about this purchase. Otherwise, the dishwasher is crap. Believe all the negative reviews about this dishwasher not drying anything. We're not talking about a little moisture here and there. When a cycle is complete, every item is soaked with water and the inside surfaces of the walls and door are sopping wet, from top to bottom. This is my third Bosch 300. I loved the first but had to replace it when a child accidentally landed on the open door. The second only lasted 5 years before the motor became noisy and occasional water on the floor made me think it had a leakage problem. Both previous Bosch dishwashers washed and dried very well, so I did not think twice before buying this one. I certainly didn't think I needed to read ALL the reviews. Why manufacturers don't think a dishwasher needs to dry dishes is beyond me. Even with the door wide open after running a cycle, I don't think 24 hours would be enough to dry the dishes and the interior surfaces of this dishwasher. (Installation date: 11/6/23)

Sentence (English): After YEARS of tears, frustration, and way too much money spent on repair bills to try and get our family's dishes cleaned in my previous dishwasher that had the word "Kitchen" in it, I had had enough!
Comments (English): [ Bosch I Never Knew Dishes Could Get So Clean ] || ---------------- || After YEARS of tears, frustration, and way too much money spent on repair bills to try and get our family's dishes cleaned in my previous dishwasher that had the word "Kitchen" in it, I had had enough! I was exhausted from washing and rewashing dishes. To my embarrassment, guests knew they had to feel inside cups and glasses to see if there was grit or grime. In Consumer Reports, Bosch emerged as the clear winner! As soon as my Bosch was delivered, I couldn't wait to wash my first load of dishes. Did I really not need to rinse and scrub my dishes first? Loading the dishwasher was pure joy. The racks were nicely laid out. Amazing top utensil rack! After adding rinse aid and detergent, I set my preferences and closed the door. The dishwasher was so quiet that I wondered if it was even running. Seeing the red triangle on the floor reaffirmed that it was fine. Opening the door after the load was complete, I took a deep breath. The moment I started feeling the dishes, I felt my jaw drop open. I was amazed at how clear and shiny the glasses were. Grit-free! Everything was spotless. As I shrieked in delight, everyone rushed in. Come look at it, I told everyone. Even my teenagers were taken aback by the shine and sparkle of the dishes. The dishes had never looked this clean before, they said. Having owned my Bosch dishwasher for two months now, I am still amazed at how well it cleans. This is every time I open that door at the end of the cycle. Thank you Bosch for making one chore that I and my children don't particularly enjoy much more enjoyable. I would like to thank you for making such a high-quality kitchen product.

Sentence (English): I wanted to buy a Triple Care dishwasher because the kitchen space was small, but I was happy to be able to buy a SK Magic dishwasher even if I could only fit a few dishes by purchasing a smaller, ultra-slim dishwasher because of the TV over the sink.
Comments (English): [ I wanted to buy the Triple Care dishwasher because the kitchen space is small, but I was happy to be able to buy the SK Magic dishwasher even if I could only fit a few dishes by purchasing a smaller, ultra-slim dishwasher because of the TV over the sink. ] || ---------------- || I wanted to buy a Triple Care dishwasher because the kitchen space was small, but I was happy to be able to buy a SK Magic dishwasher even if I could only fit a few dishes by purchasing a smaller, ultra-slim dishwasher because of the TV over the sink. But I can't turn the TV monitor sideways and use it, so why did I buy something so small? Advantages: Even if a few dishes accumulate, they can be washed immediately, so the dish turnover rate is good. When I collect it and wash it, it feels a bit uncomfortable because there is dirt in the dishwasher, odor, and dirt inside the dishes, but it is good that there is no such thing. Disadvantages: Plastic does not dry well, the top compartment is sometimes difficult to clean, and water appears in the hollow area on the back of the bowl. In addition, transparent water cups have water stains, so if you want a shiny glass cup, you must wipe them *****, and the inside of the dishwasher must be wiped every few days when there is some moisture to keep the inside clean. I contacted AS and found out that if the dishwasher is not broken, it cannot be returned, so you need to choose carefully if you don't want to throw it away.

Sentence (English): I ordered a dishwasher for my mother's house while remodeling!
Comments (English): [ Installation completed at mother's house ] || ---------------- || I ordered a dishwasher for my mother's house while remodeling! It came in a variety of colors, so I matched it to the color of the sink, and it was a perfect fit! It cleans well, and on days when we have a lot of guests, having a dishwasher makes things a little more convenient. One thing I didn't like about this product is that the buttons are coated with something like glass, making them hard to see when light reflects off them. My mother complained, so I printed out some labels and attached them to her. Also, the remaining time display disappears when the door is closed, making it practically useless. Still, I can turn it on and go about my day, so it's not a huge inconvenience. Oh, and when you order the dishwasher, your in-laws come first to inspect the sink before installing it. Even if you plan the installation in advance, they always come to check, and the installer usually comes the next day. Both the installer and the installer were incredibly friendly. Please keep this in mind when purchasing. :)
Comments (Original): [ 어머님 댁에 설치 완료 ] || ---------------- || 어머님 집에 리모델링하면서 식기세척기 주문해드렸어요!컬러가 다양해서 싱크대 장 색깔과 맞춰 주문했는데 찰떡이더라구요!세척력 좋고, 집에 손님 많이 오는날엔 식기세척기 있으니 조금 더 편하신 것 같더라구요.이 제품의 아쉬운 점이라면, 버튼 누르는 부분이 유리코팅(?) 처럼 되어 있어서 빛이 반사되면 잘 보이지 않아요.어머님이 잘 안보인다고 하셔서 라벨테이프로 출력해 붙여드렸어요.그리고 남은 시간 표시 부분이 문을 닫으면 보이질 않아 사실상 의미가 없다는 점..그래도 돌려놓고 다른일 하다보면 어느샌가 다 돌아가 있으니 큰 불편함은 아닌 것 같아요.아 그리고 제품 신청하면 먼저 식기세척기 설치할 수 있도록 싱크대장을 보러 와주시는 시가님이 먼저 오세요.미리 맞춰 장을 짜놓았어도 확인차 꼭 오시고, 보통 그 다음날 설치기사님이 오시는 것 같더라구요.싱크대장 기사님도 설치기사님도 엄청 친절하셨어요:)구매하실 분들 참고하셔서 구매하셔요:)

Sentence (English): The dishwasher I have been looking forward to for a long time did not disappoint me.
Comments (English): The dishwasher I have been looking forward to for a long time did not disappoint me. I was hesitant after reading a lot of negative reviews, but then I decided to buy it after a friend who was using it strongly recommended it. The order placed on the 2nd showed delivery on the 7th, and Panasonic called on the 5th to inquire about the installation time. Booked for the 8th. After installing it, I couldn't wait to wash it once. After strong washing and drying, except for a slight problem with the placement of the snow pan and a stain that was not removed, everything else was perfect. The glass is shiny and uses the condensed beads that come with the box. Because they were washed too clean, the coating on the outside of the chopsticks was washed away. I just found out that chopsticks are plated. But it doesn't matter, as long as I don't need to wash it, it will fall off if it falls off. The wooden handle of the Xueping pot is fine visually. I wonder if it will cause problems if it is washed too much. I am very satisfied with the fact that the pot can be put in. I applaud.
Comments (Original): 期待了很久的洗碗机，果然没让我失望。之前看了很多黑评一度犹豫，后来还是正在用的朋友极力推荐才下定决心买回来。2号下单显示7号送达，5号松下就打电话来询问安装时间。预定在8号。装完迫不及待的洗了一次。强洗带烘干，除了雪平锅放置的位置略有问题，一块污渍没洗掉，其他的堪称完美。玻璃杯闪闪发亮，用的是随箱赠送的凝珠。由于洗的太干净，筷子外部的镀层都被洗掉了。我竟然刚知道筷子是镀了一层的。但是不要紧，只要不用我洗，掉了就掉了。雪平锅的木质手柄目测没问题，不知道洗多了会不会有问题，锅能放进去这点让我很满意，鼓掌

Sentence (English): I have been disappointed in this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Disappointing ] || ---------------- || I have been disappointed in this dishwasher. The controls are not intuitive, and the instructions in the "Quick Start" guide are of limited help. (Further adding to my frustration is that a complete user guide does not come with the dishwasher, but rather is only available online.) When I try to start the dishwasher, it often simply shuts down. It turns out that in order to start the unit, you first have to turn it off and then turn it back on. Then you have to select your cycle and options. THEN you have to press "Start." Really? Adding insult to injury, any time you open the dishwasher to add a dish after the cycle has already started, you again need to press the "Start" button. It should start automatically upon re-closing the door. And I can't figure out the digital display at all. The number of minutes displayed seems random and can vary from 200+ to 40-50, with the displayed number of minutes seeming to have no correspondence with the cycle and/or options selected. And don't get me started on making selections of optional features, such as the bottom-mounted light. It takes a Ph.D in visual interpretation to figure out how to adjust these features. The Bosch engineers need to go back to the drawing board on the design of these features. My inexpensive prior dishwasher was far easier to use, even though it had many of the same features as this Bosch.

There's only 2 of us in my household so we only run it once a week. The rinse aid leaks all over when you put it in. Everyone told me Bosch is great but I definitely am having second thoughts about my purchase. I will try the normal and heavy cycles to see if they work any better. It is quiet, but if it doesn't clean good, what good is that? Not impressed at all so far.

Comments (English): [ Fraud and customer service nightmare ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher for $498 from Home Depot. It was delivered by a contractor in a crate that was undamaged. It took me almost a week to find an installer who opened the crate and found the unit badly damaged. I contacted Home Depot who denied all responsibility and insisted that the damage and fraudulent packaging was the fault of LG. I spent many, many hours on the phone, via email, and on the LG "customer service" chat line, trying to get them to refund my money so I can shop for a new dishwasher. LG "escalated" my case the first day, but now almost three weeks later I still have an obviously smashed dishwasher in the middle of the kitchen floor and ABSOLUTELY NOTHING from LG.LG sold a badly-damaged product as brand new, fraudulently repackaging the unit to hide the obvious damage. Then they gave me weeks and weeks of runaround. I dutifully sent them all my information over and over, providing proofs of purchase, photos of the damage, and repeatedly sent photos of very specific parts and interior labels of the product. Nevertheless, they refuse to respond to my requests for a refund. I am aghast at both LGs fraudulent attempt to hide the obvious damage and sell this product as new, and even worse at the complete lack of customer service under their warranty.Of course I will never purchase any LG product again, either for myself or for the rental houses I own and manage.

Sentence (English): We are a family of 4 that does lots of cooking and we run the dishwasher daily.
Comments (English): [ Best dishwasher I've ever owned ] || ---------------- || We are a family of 4 that does lots of cooking and we run the dishwasher daily. I have thrown everything I can at this machine and everything has come out clean. We scrape but never rinse. Gunk caked on pots. Crust in the corners of baking dishes. I've so far been unable to stump this dishwasher. I love the interior light, floor timer light, and water softener. The app lets you know when things are wrong (out of salt, out of rinse aid, something blocking the lower spin arm). Dishes come out sparkling clean and dry every time. And it's basically silent. This dishwasher is well worth the money.I have a few small gripes that are all related to the human interface team. A) The power button provides no visual, audio, or mechanical feedback until 1 to 2 seconds after you press it. That's just enough time to make me think I didn't press it correctly. But inevitably a 2nd press turns it back off. It's stupid. B) The app takes quite a bit of time to connect to the dishwasher and often it just will not connect at all. Sometimes turning on the dishwasher will help. Sometimes resetting the dishwasher will help. Other times I just give up. C) There is no delay start button on the dishwasher, you must use the app for that. The app has lots of time features: delay start, specific time start, and run during a specific time of day. But it's a pain to start my dishwasher via the app every single day. A normal delay button that cycles through some delay hours would be nice. D) A fully programable "custom" button on the dishwasher would be great. I almost always use the exact same settings for every load. But that includes a time-of-day range setting that can only be added via the app. I can program the app with a favorite cycle and time of day but I cannot link that to a button on the dishwasher.All of those gripes pale in comparison to how amazing the dishwasher is though. My dirty stuff comes out clean. Amazing!

Sentence (English): I hope this will be helpful for you in purchasing the dishwasher you needed after moving.
Comments (English): [ Recommended for small households without installation ] || ---------------- || I hope this will be helpful for you in purchasing the dishwasher you needed after moving. Please read the content even though it is a bit long. I will write honestly. I thought it would be big because it is for 2-3 people, but it is really big when I actually received it. I thought it was about the size of a microwave, but you can't feel it in the picture. The size in the manual is 43.5 in height, 42 in width, and 43.5 in length, and 14 kg. When I measured it with a tape measure, it was 43.5 in height, 41 in width, and 41 in length. There may be a 1-2 cm error range depending on the person measuring. The drain line is long, so you can cut it to fit your use. A family of two I am a couple without children. We are both big eaters, so we mainly use large plates and bowls. I think it is perfect for a family of two. Including 4 soup bowls, side dish plates, 3-4 bowls, spoons, chopsticks, and cups are enough. The manual says to arrange the bowls straight, but it is better to place them diagonally. Since it sprays water above and below, the entire bowl touches the water, making it easy to wash. Good thing I mostly eat home-cooked meals. The cups were the most troublesome. I first sorted the cups before washing the dishes, but there was a peculiar fishy smell. Sometimes, even after rinsing them with hot water, the smell persists. Next, the oily dishes and plates, but when I looked at the results, there was no smell of the dirty dishes and cups. It was fun to fill them up one by one as if playing Tetris while putting the dishes and cups in. It is easy to install because it is non-porous. Overall review: It is a bit of a hassle to have to pour water one by one, but my husband and I, a family of two who often eat home-cooked meals and are sensitive to smells, were satisfied because it got rid of the fishy smell from the oily water cups. The price is reasonable at 200,000 won, and it is easy to access because it is non-porous. I put it in front, but I am going to use it and turn it to the side again. Sentence (English): My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Really,,, oh my,,, a yellowish white that has turned yellow from being exposed to the sun for a long time,,,,,,;;;;;;; continue.

These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Sentence (English): Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort.
Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better.
