Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. Comments (English): [ For my wrists and finger joints ] || ---------------- || My husband asked me if I was using a mini dishwasher. I was so touched that I exclaimed, "Even a cat's paw would be so helpful, but this dishwasher and the robot vacuum are the only things that care for me in this house!" Sometimes, I'd stack the dishes to ensure even water flow, and then, as time flew by, I'd think I'd already finished washing them, and then I'd get a realization: time had passed, but my wrists and knuckles hadn't been used as much. I'd say I'd only washed a few dishes, but my finger joints were aching, and my wrists were starting to feel worse. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better. These days, I'm thinking the best way to protect my cartilage is to avoid wearing it down. Washing dishes was painful and frustrating, so I bought a mini dishwasher as a last resort. While it has its limitations, I'm satisfied. If you're reading reviews, I urge you to buy it now. I've been using it for over three weeks now, and I've switched between Ever Zero tablet detergent and Super Bubble liquid detergent. At first, I was worried that the detergent might stain the dish, but I divided it into 12 portions instead of 4, and it didn't leave any marks and the dishes washed cleanly. I chop it up finely and adjust it according to the amount of dishes I use. The liquid detergent is supposed to be used for 6 people, so I put it in a plastic bottle for children and squeezed out about 3ml at a time, and the dishes were washed cleanly. Don't buy conditioner. I ordered it when I bought it, but I returned it. The Minix dishwasher doesn't have a separate detergent compartment; it sits on the bottom, so you can't use conditioner. That's why you should use one of the new all-in-one products. I bought the conditioner because I heard it was good for removing stains, but I canceled it, but the silicone lid stains no matter what detergent I use. Glass containers and stainless steel pots are cleaned sparklingly, just like with detergent. The cutlery holder can be stacked on two levels, and you can put spoons and cooking utensils on top. After using it for a few days, it felt a little uncomfortable, and when I stacked them on top, there were parts where the water didn't flow, so I bought an LG dishwasher cutlery holder and inserted it in the middle, and it somehow fits securely. If the back part is not stacked correctly, it can fall down and the rotating blades underneath can't turn, but since there's a middle support, it's easy to stack and it feels like it can hold more. I think there's a little misunderstanding about the door opening part! I naturally thought the door would open automatically after washing and drying with hot air. However, when I wash it normally, it washes for 1 hour and dries for 2 hours. After washing for 1 hour, it opens, waits for a few minutes, then closes again to dry for 2 hours. And the door doesn't open automatically again! So when I turn it on before work, I either press the storage button to wash it and leave, or when the 1-hour wash is done, I turn it off and leave the door wide open. If I just close the door after washing, the window gets humid. So I use tweezers to keep it from closing completely. The interior light turns off after a few minutes, but the front window's open button doesn't turn off. So, I ordered a single-outlet outlet. I want to be able to immediately turn off the power without unplugging the cord when I'm done washing. When I first received the product, the box was tattered, so I was worried it might be a return. There were also scratches on the water tank, which I was concerned might break it, and there was water inside the product, so I called customer service. They told me that, while not all products are like this, they do have a label stating that they test the product before shipping to prevent malfunctions. They also said the water tank couldn't be exchanged separately, so I decided to just use it. The box was so huge that I couldn't even think about exchanging it. It's supposed to be quiet, but it's not unbearably loud, either. It's as noisy as a mini washing machine or spin dryer running inside the house. I've attached a video so you can listen. I can hear the noise coming from the front door. I saw on YouTube that they recommend stacking dishes and turning the top and bottom spinning plates to see if they're spinning. Since it is a transparent window, you need to check if the water stream is spinning and spraying in the middle. Sometimes, the water stream gets stuck in the gap below and doesn't go back, and there were a few times when the upper water stream turning plate was fixed even though there was definitely nothing blocking it, so I stopped it and tried spinning it again by hand and pressed the wash button again, and it worked fine that time. I think you need to check once in a while if the water stream is spraying properly. And the color is a modern gray,,,, but maybe because I am old-fashioned, I think white like the water purifier next to it would be better.
